concepts.title: Harness Sync Engine
concepts.description: 3366-line bash engine that pulls upstream harness domains via GitHub tarball while preserving fork renames, substitutions, and protected files.
concepts.notes: scripts/sync-claude-harness.sh, 3366 lines, 57 functions, set -e | 10 commands dispatched by case on $1: init|status|version|diff|sync|manifest|rollback|conflicts|releases|help | check_dependencies + migrate_metadata_to_root run for every command except help | hard deps: curl, node, python3 (python3 only for YAML->JSON via PyYAML; missing python3 or PyYAML => print_warning + HAS_MANIFEST=false, silent degrade to legacy) | metadata at repo root (v2.10.0+): .harness-sync.json, .harness-backup/, .harness-patches/, .harness-manifest.yml, .harness-manifest.schema.json; legacy .claude/ copies auto-copied forward by migrate_metadata_to_root and left in place | .sync-exclude and .sync-exclude.default stay under .claude/ (legacy fallback only) | tmp workspace /tmp/claude-harness-sync-$$, rm -rf on EXIT trap | fetch_upstream: curl -sL https://api.github.com/repos/$UPSTREAM_REPO/tarball/$ref piped to tar xz --strip-components=1; ABORTS if $TMP_DIR/.claude absent even when sync_scope excludes .claude | get_upstream_sha / get_latest_release / list_releases hit api.github.com unauthenticated | do_sync pipeline per domain: apply_all_substitutions(DOMAIN_TMP) -> build sync_plan (is_excluded -> resolve_rename -> compare_file_with_paths) -> run_preflight -> create_backup -> cp substituted TMP file over local | substitution happens in TMP_DIR BEFORE preflight so the token scanner sees post-substitution state | create_backup writes .harness-backup/<domain>/<SYNC_TIMESTAMP>/, prunes to last 3 timestamps per domain; SYNC_TIMESTAMP shared across all domains in one run so do_rollback can restore every domain from one timestamp | do_rollback picks newest timestamp via date -d (GNU-only flag; returns 0 epoch on BSD date) and copies back into $PROJECT_ROOT/<domain>/ | update_sync_metadata writes BOTH key families: last_synced_commit/last_synced_version/last_synced_at AND last_sync_commit/last_sync_version/last_sync_timestamp, plus sync_history capped at 10 | flags: --dry-run --version <tag> --latest --scope <csv> --no-placeholders --skip-preflight --generate-patches; unknown args silently shifted, never error | no manifest + no --dry-run => print_error + return 1; with --dry-run => warns and previews with legacy .claude-only scope | REQUIRES BASH 4: do_diff line 1560 'declare -A dir_rename_counts' + line 1702 ${!arr[@]}; on macOS /bin/bash 3.2 do_diff dies with 'declare: -A: invalid option' and produces no output - this is the single root cause of 12/50 failures in tests/test-rename-diff.sh, 6/54 in tests/test-protected-files.sh, and 7 failures in tests/test-fork-sync.sh | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.conflict_strategy (upstream-wins|local-wins|prompt|three-way) is only READ for display in do_status line 2453; no branch anywhere implements it - do_sync unconditionally cp's upstream over local (de-facto upstream-wins) and the conflicts counter passed to update_sync_metadata is hardcoded 0 | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.auto_substitute documented as 'Set to false to sync raw upstream files' is never read; only --no-placeholders suppresses substitution | DOC DRIFT: manifest sync.substitution_extensions is never read; apply_all_substitutions hardcodes .md .json .yml .yaml .sh .py .txt .toml .ts .mjs .bib .cff (.bib/.cff extra vs the manifest list) | DOC DRIFT: manifest 'replaced' section documented to skip files and log 'Skipped (replaced): <path>' - that string does not exist in the script; get_protected_patterns reads only data.protected, so 'replaced' entries are counted in status/validate output and otherwise OVERWRITTEN | DOC DRIFT: show_help says both 'sync requires a manifest ... sync will fail' and 'Without a manifest, the script uses legacy file-level copy behavior' | is_protected falls back to substring match after glob match, so a short protected pattern silently protects unrelated paths | do_conflicts only scans $CLAUDE_DIR for *.conflict, ignoring other sync domains | UNKNOWN: is any *.conflict file ever written? no writer for that suffix found in the script

concepts.title: Harness Manifest Schema
concepts.description: JSON Schema plus template YAML declaring how a downstream fork customizes the harness: identity, substitutions, renames, protected, replaced, sync prefs.
concepts.notes: schema draft 2020-12, additionalProperties:false at root, required [manifest_version, identity] | 7 top-level sections: manifest_version, identity, substitutions, renames, protected, replaced, sync | repo's own .harness-manifest.yml is manifest_version 1.1 with 27 identity keys all still {{PLACEHOLDER}} values, empty substitutions/renames/protected/replaced, sync_scope listing all 6 allowed domains | schema required identity subset: PROJECT_NAME PROJECT_REPO PROJECT_SHORT GITHUB_ORG TICKET_PREFIX MAIN_BRANCH (6 of 27) | identity key names mirror scripts/setup-template.sh {{...}} tokens exactly | v1.0 = paths relative to .claude/, v1.1+ = repo-root-relative; do_sync sets USE_ROOT_PATHS=true when manifest_version is 1.1 or lexically greater and prefixes $CURRENT_DOMAIN/ onto every manifest lookup key | renames: trailing / marks a directory rename; resolve_rename checks exact file match first, then directory prefix match, then passthrough (file wins over directory) | ENFORCEMENT GAP vs schema: validate_manifest is hand-rolled bash+node, NOT a JSON Schema validator - it checks only manifest_version regex ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$, presence of identity plus the 6 required subkeys, and emits WARNINGS (never errors) for absolute or .. rename paths; schema patterns for TICKET_PREFIX (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}$), PROJECT_REPO, substitutions propertyNames, sync_scope enum, additionalProperties:false, and format:email/uri are NEVER enforced at runtime | malformed YAML is not fatal: load_manifest prints 'Falling back to legacy sync' and sets HAS_MANIFEST=false | sync_scope enum in schema is duplicated as bash ALLOWED_DOMAINS=(.claude .gemini .codex .cursor .agents dark-factory) at line 57 - two hardcoded copies that must be kept in step | DOC DRIFT: schema $id and description both say the manifest lives at '.claude/.harness-manifest.yml'; the script's MANIFEST_FILE is $PROJECT_ROOT/.harness-manifest.yml with .claude/ only a legacy fallback | DOC DRIFT: schema sync.backup description says 'Current: .claude/.harness-backup/. Planned (SAW-34): .harness-backup/ at repo root'; BACKUP_DIR is already the repo root and .harness-manifest.yml's own comment says repo root | DOC DRIFT: schema documents sync.backup, sync.auto_substitute, sync.conflict_strategy, sync.substitution_extensions with defaults; none of the four is read by the sync engine (only sync_scope, and conflict_strategy for display only)

concepts.title: Multi-Domain Sync Scope Resolution
concepts.description: How the sync engine resolves which harness directories to sync, from manifest sync_scope, a --scope override, or the .claude default.
concepts.notes: resolution order: get_sync_scope() reads manifest -> optional --scope <csv> override replaces it wholesale -> empty result falls back to SYNC_SCOPE=(.claude) | get_sync_scope does NOT use the parsed manifest JSON; it re-reads the raw YAML line-by-line with grep/sed looking for '^\s*sync_scope:' then consuming following '-' lines, stripping quotes and trailing slash - so a sync_scope in JSON-style flow syntax or unusual indentation is silently missed and the default applies | 6 ALLOWED_DOMAINS hardcoded at line 57: .claude .gemini .codex .cursor .agents dark-factory; anything else prints '[WARN] Ignoring unknown sync domain: X' and is dropped, not an error | --scope validates against the same allowlist; if every entry is invalid it is the ONE scope path that hard-fails (print_error + return 1); --scope never rewrites .harness-manifest.yml | domains are processed sequentially in a for loop; a domain is SKIPPED with a warning when absent from the fetched upstream tarball OR absent locally (v2.10.0 does not auto-create local domain dirs) | preflight failure inside the loop does `continue` - it skips only that domain and the sync proceeds to the next one; the process still exits 0 | per-domain state carried by globals DOMAIN_DIR / DOMAIN_TMP / CURRENT_DOMAIN, consumed by compare_file_with_paths, generate_patch, run_preflight and create_backup | SYNC_TIMESTAMP is reset once per do_sync and shared by every domain backup so rollback restores the whole set together | patches dir is created once outside the loop; APPLY_ORDER.md is generated after the loop so entries from all domains accumulate | release domains (docs/, scripts/, patterns_library/) are explicitly not in the allowlist | DOC DRIFT: fetch_upstream hard-errors 'No .claude directory found in upstream repository' regardless of sync_scope, so a fork scoped to only .gemini/ still cannot sync if upstream lacks .claude | DOC DRIFT: run_preflight's scope-violation error string is hardcoded 'files outside .claude/ would be modified' even in multi-domain runs

concepts.title: Test Suite - Preflight and Provenance
concepts.description: 18 tests, 45 assertions covering preflight scope, protected and token checks plus sync provenance; asserts real failure paths.
concepts.notes: SAW-2 | 18 numbered tests, 45 assertions, observed result exit 0 / 45 pass 0 fail on bash 3.2 | PROVES FAILURE: yes, the strongest negative suite in the repo - Test 5 scope violation, Test 6 protected violation, Test 7 unreplaced token, Test 15 absolute path, Test 17 all three at once, each asserting 'PREFLIGHT_RESULT: fail' plus the specific error string | positive controls: Test 4 clean plan passes, Test 14 empty plan passes, Test 3 non-manifest {{tokens}} are ignored | Test 8 --skip-preflight bypass, Test 10 --no-placeholders suppresses only the token check, Test 9 asserts preflight runs on real sync not just --dry-run | Tests 11-13 assert provenance in .harness-sync.json via assert_json_field/assert_json_not_null: sync_history capped at 10, ISO 8601 timestamp | strategy: unit tests source the script through a wrapper that strips the trailing case dispatch; integration tests run a mocked copy with fetch_upstream/get_upstream_sha stubbed - no network | helpers: strip_ansi, assert_contains, assert_not_contains, assert_exit_code, assert_file_exists, assert_file_content, assert_json_field, assert_json_not_null | does NOT exercise do_diff, so it never hits the bash-4 declare -A defect

concepts.title: Test Suite - Protected File Enforcement
concepts.description: 19 tests, 54 assertions on is_protected, is_manifest_protected and .sync-exclude merging; 6 fail on bash 3.2 via do_diff.
concepts.notes: SAW-3 | 19 numbered tests, 54 assertions, observed result exit 1 / 48 pass 6 FAIL on bash 3.2 | the 6 failures are all do_diff tests (Tests 7, 8, 12) expecting PROTECTED/EXCLUDED labels; root cause is 'declare -A dir_rename_counts' at sync-claude-harness.sh line 1560 which bash 3.2 rejects - the tests assert a real product requirement and the product is genuinely broken on that shell | PROVES FAILURE: partially - Test 9 asserts protected files are byte-identical after a real do_sync (a true negative outcome), Test 11 asserts the 'Protected pattern does not match any local file' typo warning; the remaining assertions are positive is_protected/is_excluded returns | coverage: manifest patterns (T1), globs incl. ** recursive (T2, T14), is_excluded delegation (T3), .sync-exclude-only fallback (T4), merged sources (T5), de-duplication (T6), manifest-vs-exclude distinction (T13), hardcoded exclusions always apply (T15), empty protected section is inert (T19), no-manifest backward compat (T12) | Test 16 is bash -n syntax only; Test 17 shells out to tests/test-manifest-loader.sh - a nested-suite dependency that makes this suite fail if the loader suite fails | does NOT test the 'replaced' section at all, which is why the unenforced-replaced gap is invisible here

concepts.title: Test Suite - Rename Resolution and Diff
concepts.description: 18 tests, 50 assertions on resolve_rename, rename_type and rename-aware diff; 12 fail on bash 3.2 because do_diff cannot run.
concepts.notes: 18 numbered tests, 50 assertions, observed result exit 1 / 38 pass 12 FAIL on bash 3.2 | all 12 failures are do_diff assertions (Tests 7, 9, 10, 11, 15) - RENAMED summary lines, 'local (upstream: X)' display paths, directory file counts, LOCAL ONLY detection; single root cause 'declare -A dir_rename_counts' at sync-claude-harness.sh line 1560 under bash 3.2 | the passing 38 are pure-function tests: file rename exact match (T1), directory prefix rename (T2), passthrough (T3), no-manifest passthrough (T4), file-beats-directory precedence (T5), rename_type classification (T6), compare_file_with_paths across differing paths (T14), do_sync placing files at renamed targets (T16), do_status rename listing (T12, T13) | PROVES FAILURE: weakly - assert_not_contains x7 and assert_file_not_exists x3 assert that the pre-rename upstream name is NOT created, which is a genuine negative; no test asserts a nonzero exit code or an error message | Test 17 is bash -n only; Test 18 shells out to tests/test-manifest-loader.sh (nested dependency)

concepts.title: Test Suite - Placeholder Substitution
concepts.description: 15 tests on apply_substitutions ordering, literals and text-file filtering; aborts mid-run under set -e when its nested rename-diff suite fails.
concepts.notes: SAW-10 | 15 numbered tests, observed result exit 1 - the suite ABORTS inside Test 14 'Existing tests still pass', which shells out to tests/test-manifest-loader.sh (passes) then tests/test-rename-diff.sh (fails on bash 3.2); set -e at the top kills the run before Test 15 and before any results summary is printed | so on bash 3.2 this suite produces NO pass/fail totals at all - its failure is inherited from the nested suite, not from a substitution defect | PROVES FAILURE: yes for the manifest gate - Test 8 asserts sync without a manifest emits 'No manifest found' and routes the user to 'manifest init'; assert_file_not_contains x4 and assert_not_contains x6 assert tokens are ABSENT after substitution | coverage: {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens (T1), longest-match-first ordering so {{GITHUB_REPO_URL}} beats {{GITHUB_ORG}} (T2), code examples not clobbered (T3), literal-string substitutions (T4), --no-placeholders skip (T5), backup retains pre-substitution upstream originals (T6), full sync integration (T7), empty substitutions section is inert (T9), special characters (T10), missing file handled gracefully (T11), apply_all_substitutions text-extension filter (T12) | Test 13 is bash -n only; Test 15 greps help text for --no-placeholders | does NOT test that sync.auto_substitute is honoured, which is why the unread-auto_substitute gap is invisible here

concepts.title: Test Suite - Patch Generation Mode
concepts.description: 17 tests, 50 assertions on --generate-patches output, rename and substitution awareness, and git apply compatibility; all pass.
concepts.notes: SAW-4 | 17 numbered tests, 50 assertions, observed result exit 0 / 50 pass 0 fail on bash 3.2 | PROVES FAILURE: weakly - no test asserts a nonzero exit code or an error string; the negative evidence is behavioural: Test 6 asserts protected files produce NO patch, Test 7 asserts no local file is overwritten in patch mode, Test 13 asserts unchanged files produce no patch, Test 17 asserts no backup directory is created; plus assert_file_not_content x5 for absent tokens | Test 15 is the only externally-validated assertion: it initialises a real git repo and runs 'git apply --check' on a generated patch, so patch validity is proven rather than string-matched | other coverage: patch files land in .harness-patches/<version>/ (T1, T11), unified-diff shape (T2, assert_patch_valid), APPLY_ORDER.md generated and categorised NEW vs UPDATED (T3, T10), rename-aware headers using the fork's local path (T4), substitution-aware content (T5, T14), new files diff against /dev/null (T8), modified diff correctness (T9), stale patches for the same version are rm -rf'd first (T12), filename sanitisation slash to __ (T16) | strategy: mocked sync script with network stubs; no network | does NOT exercise do_diff, so it avoids the bash-4 declare -A defect

concepts.title: Test Suite - Manifest Loader and Validator
concepts.description: 12 tests, 24 assertions on load_manifest and validate_manifest; asserts every required-field error message and the invalid-YAML fallback.
concepts.notes: SAW-6 | 12 numbered tests, 24 assertions, observed result exit 0 / 24 pass 0 fail on bash 3.2 | PROVES FAILURE: yes - Test 3 asserts 'missing required field: manifest_version', Test 4 asserts 'must match pattern X.Y', Test 5 asserts 'missing required field: PROJECT_REPO' and 'missing required field: TICKET_PREFIX', Test 6 asserts 'missing required field: identity', Test 12 asserts invalid YAML produces 'Falling back to legacy' | Test 12 therefore LOCKS IN the silent-degrade behaviour: a corrupt manifest is treated as no manifest rather than as an error | other coverage: no-manifest legacy fallback (T1, T9), valid manifest parse (T2), summary report format (T7), zero counts for empty sections (T8), manifest block in status output (T10), .harness-manifest.yml is always excluded from sync (T11) | the required-identity assertions cover only 2 of the 6 required keys (PROJECT_REPO, TICKET_PREFIX); PROJECT_NAME, PROJECT_SHORT, GITHUB_ORG, MAIN_BRANCH are not individually asserted | this suite is invoked as a nested dependency by tests/test-protected-files.sh, tests/test-rename-diff.sh and tests/test-substitutions.sh | does NOT assert any schema constraint that validate_manifest omits (TICKET_PREFIX pattern, enum values, additionalProperties), so the validator/schema divergence is untested

concepts.title: Test Suite - Manifest Init Wizard
concepts.description: 14 tests, 52 assertions on manifest init generation from team-config, .sync-exclude and detected domains; all pass.
concepts.notes: SAW-12 | 14 numbered tests, 52 assertions, observed result exit 0 / 52 pass 0 fail on bash 3.2 | PROVES FAILURE: weakly - Test 5 asserts the 'No team-config.json' warning, Test 9 asserts 'No manifest found' from manifest validate on a missing file, Test 8 asserts overwrite protection prompts; assert_file_not_exists x2 and assert_not_contains x2 are the only other negatives; no nonzero-exit assertion anywhere | coverage: --dry-run prints without writing (T1), --yes writes the file (T2), .sync-exclude becomes the protected section (T3), unreplaced {{...}} team-config values are recognised as placeholders (T4, T13), substitutions populated (T6), generated manifest re-validates (T7), manifest subcommand help (T10), derived values TICKET_PREFIX_LOWER/AUTHOR_INITIALS/GITHUB_REPO_URL/HARNESS_VERSION computed (T11), sync preferences block emitted (T12), MCP server names detected (T14) | Test 7 'validates against schema' actually re-runs the script's own validate_manifest, not a JSON Schema validator - it proves self-consistency, not schema conformance | domain auto-detection (do_manifest_init step 4 scanning ALLOWED_DOMAINS for existing directories) has no dedicated test | the wizard reads .claude/team-config.json for identity - one of the few places it is coupled to the .claude domain specifically

concepts.title: Test Suite - Multi-Domain Sync
concepts.description: 14 tests on sync_scope, root-relative paths, shared timestamps and cross-domain rollback; aborts at Test 1 on BSD head.
concepts.notes: SAW-37 | 14 numbered tests, observed result exit 1 - ABORTS inside Test 1 with 'head: illegal line count -- -3' | root cause: make_sourceable() at line 68 uses 'head -n -3' (GNU-only negative line count) to strip the script's case dispatch; BSD/macOS head rejects it and set -euo pipefail kills the run immediately, so ZERO tests execute on macOS | this is an environment defect in the test harness, not in sync_scope | PROVES FAILURE (by source inspection, unverified by execution here): Test 3 asserts invalid domains are dropped with 'Ignoring unknown sync domain' while valid ones survive; Test 4 asserts manifest-required enforcement | intended coverage: get_sync_scope reads v1.1 sync_scope (T1), defaults to .claude for v1.0 (T2), invalid-domain rejection (T3), manifest-required (T4), USE_ROOT_PATHS flag for v1.1 (T5), metadata migration .claude to root (T6), ALLOWED_DOMAINS list contents (T7), v1.1 protected-path enforcement outside .claude (T8), root-relative file+directory rename resolution (T9), compare_file_with_paths domain context (T10), SYNC_TIMESTAMP shared across domain backups (T11), validate_protected_paths across multiple domains (T12), do_rollback restoring all domains from one timestamp (T13), real multi-domain patch generation with APPLY_ORDER.md (T14) | only 43 assertions total (39 assert_contains, 3 assert_equals, 1 assert_not_contains) - a single negative assertion for 14 tests, so even when it runs it is overwhelmingly a positive-path suite | UNKNOWN: does this suite pass on a GNU-coreutils Linux runner? not verifiable from this machine

concepts.title: Test Suite - Fork Compatibility
concepts.description: 18 sub-tests running real sync commands against the rendertrust and keryk-ai fixtures; currently fails and aborts on a missing fixture file.
concepts.notes: SAW-9 | 18 sub-tests in 4 groups (1.x RenderTrust, 2.x Keryk AI, 3.x error handling, 4.x fixture integrity) | OBSERVED STATE: exit 1, 28 PASS then hard ABORT at line 596 - 'cat: .../ka-protected/.claude/settings.local.json: No such file or directory' under set -e; the keryk-ai fixture directory has no settings.local.json but Test 2.5 cats it as a baseline; Tests 2.6, 3.1-3.4 and all of group 4 never execute | SECOND independent defect: 7 assertions in Tests 1.2 and 2.2 already FAIL before the abort because do_diff dies on 'declare: -A: invalid option' (bash 3.2 vs the bash-4 associative array at sync-claude-harness.sh line 1560) | PROVES FAILURE: yes, group 3 is the only fixture-driven negative group - Test 3.1 asserts status exits 1 on an invalid manifest and names the missing identity, Test 3.2 asserts the manifest_version error; both are currently UNREACHABLE because of the abort | what still passes: manifest loading/validation for both forks, dry-run exit codes, rename resolution during real sync (fe-developer to ui-engineer, be-developer to api-engineer, data-engineer to ml-engineer, stripe-patterns/ to payment-patterns/), identity substitution, RenderTrust protected-file preservation | mechanism: setup_fork_project copies a fixture into a mktemp dir, setup_mock_upstream builds a fake upstream tree, create_stubbed_script rewrites fetch_upstream to copy from the local mock so nothing touches the network | group 4 (unreached) checks fixture manifests parse as YAML, that fixture PROJECT_NAME matches the corresponding examples/manifests/ file, and that renamed fixture files exist

concepts.title: Sync Test Fixtures and Example Manifests
concepts.description: Two synthetic fork snapshots and their published example manifests, used as the sync engine's fork-compatibility contract.
concepts.notes: 19 fixture files total: rendertrust 8 (7 under .claude/ plus .harness-manifest.yml), keryk-ai 11 (10 under .claude/ plus .harness-manifest.yml) | rendertrust = the no-rename fork: agents/be-developer.md, agents/fe-developer.md, skills/stripe-patterns/SKILL.md keep upstream names; renames: {} | keryk-ai = the rename fork: agents/ui-engineer.md, agents/api-engineer.md, agents/ml-engineer.md, skills/payment-patterns/SKILL.md, plus custom agents/ml-ops-engineer.md and a rewritten agents/system-architect.md | 2 example manifests under examples/manifests/, named <fork>.harness-manifest.yml; fixture copies differ from the examples only in leading comment blocks and inline comments - identity/renames/protected/replaced bodies match, which is what test-fork-sync group 4.2 checks (on PROJECT_NAME only) | ALL FOUR manifests are manifest_version 1.0, i.e. .claude-relative paths; nothing in the fixture set exercises the v1.1 root-relative path mode that the repo's own manifest and the current engine default to | none of the four declares sync_scope, so every fixture run resolves to the default [.claude] - there is no multi-domain fixture | keryk-ai declares conflict_strategy 'three-way' and rendertrust 'prompt'; neither is implemented by the engine, so the fixtures encode a promise the code does not keep | FIXTURE GAP: tests/fixtures/sync/keryk-ai/.claude/settings.local.json is named in that manifest's protected patterns and is cat'd by tests/test-fork-sync.sh line 596, but the file does not exist on disk - this is the abort that kills the fork-sync suite | fixture .claude/ trees contain no hooks/, commands/ or settings.json, so hook and command sync is never fixture-covered

concepts.title: setup-template.sh - Template Setup Wizard
concepts.description: Interactive one-time wizard that replaces every {{PLACEHOLDER}} token across the repo with the operator's project values.
concepts.notes: scripts/setup-template.sh, 233 lines, bash, set -euo pipefail | run once after creating a repo from the template: bash scripts/setup-template.sh | 27 interactive `read -rp` prompts grouped as Project Identity / Organization / Author / Workflow / MCP Server Names / Infrastructure; MAIN_BRANCH, MCP_LINEAR_SERVER and MCP_CONFLUENCE_SERVER offer bracketed defaults | 4 derived values computed, never prompted: TICKET_PREFIX_LOWER, AUTHOR_INITIALS, GITHUB_REPO_URL, HARNESS_VERSION | REPLACEMENTS array holds 31 token-to-value pairs, hand-ordered longest/most-specific first so {{GITHUB_REPO_URL}} is consumed before {{GITHUB_ORG}} and {{AUTHOR_FIRST_NAME}} before {{AUTHOR_NAME}}; pairs where old equals new are skipped | applies via find over 17 name patterns (*.md *.json *.yml *.yaml *.sh *.py *.txt *.toml *.bib *.cff *.mjs *.ts NOTICE LICENSE CODEOWNERS .env.template .gitignore) excluding .git and node_modules, piped through xargs -0 into _sed_inplace | _sed_inplace probes `sed --version | grep GNU` and uses `sed -i` vs `sed -i ''` - genuinely cross-platform, unlike the other doc scripts in this directory | echoes a review block and requires an explicit y at 'Proceed?' before touching anything; no backup is taken and no dry-run flag exists - the only undo is git | THIS SCRIPT IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR TOKEN NAMES: .harness-manifest.yml identity keys and .harness-manifest.schema.json both state they must match setup-template.sh exactly, and the sync engine rebuilds its substitution map from them | prompts for the DB_PASSWORD key in cleartext and writes it into tracked files | no --yes / non-interactive mode, so it cannot run in CI

concepts.title: apply-workflow.sh - Workflow Integration Installer
concepts.description: Copies the workflow template into an existing project and substitutes a second, incompatible __TOKEN__ placeholder family.
concepts.notes: scripts/apply-workflow.sh, 176 lines, bash, set -e, mode 0644 (NOT executable - must be invoked as `bash scripts/apply-workflow.sh`) | prompts for provider (1 Claude Code to .claude, 2 Augment to .augment), then TICKET_PREFIX, PRIMARY_DEV_BRANCH, PROJECT_GIT_URL, PROJECT_NAME, TICKET_URL_PREFIX; the first two are hard-required via log_error, the rest only warn | copies AGENTS.md and the directories project_workflow/, patterns_library/, specs_templates/, linting_configs/ into TARGET_DIR (hardcoded '.'), then agent_providers/<provider>/ into the provider config dir | all six referenced source directories exist on disk | substitutes FIVE tokens of a completely different family: __TICKET_PREFIX__, __PRIMARY_DEV_BRANCH__, __PROJECT_GIT_URL__, __PROJECT_NAME__, __TICKET_URL_PREFIX__ | those __TOKEN__ markers are real and live in agent_providers/augment/rules/project-guidelines.md, agent_providers/augment/AUGMENT_WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md, specs_templates/planning_template.md, specs_templates/spec_template.md, project_workflow/CONTRIBUTING.md | DOC DRIFT: this is a SECOND parallel templating system - scripts/setup-template.sh uses {{TOKEN}} and the sync manifest's substitution engine only ever matches {{...}}, so __TOKEN__ placeholders are invisible to sync and to run_preflight's unreplaced-token check | uses bare GNU `sed -i` with no backup suffix, which fails on BSD/macOS sed - unlike setup-template.sh which has a _sed_inplace shim | merges ci:validate / ci:build / ci:test into package.json with jq; when jq is absent it only prints the scripts for manual entry and continues | TEMPLATE_DIR is $(dirname $0) i.e. scripts/, so the cp sources resolve one level below the repo root - UNKNOWN: is this script expected to be copied to the repo root before running?

concepts.title: install-prompts.sh - Agent Prompt Installer
concepts.description: Installs the agent prompts for Claude Code at user or team scope, or for Augment Code.
concepts.notes: scripts/install-prompts.sh, 285 lines, bash, set -e, executable | 3 modes selected by flag, MODE defaults to 'user': --user / --team / --augment, plus --help | install_claude_user copies .claude/agents/*.md into the user-level agents dir and .claude/hooks/*.sh into the user hooks dir with `|| true` so a missing hooks dir is non-fatal | install_claude_team uses the in-project .claude/agents as-is for team sharing (no copy out) | install_augment sources agent_providers/augment | source dirs: CLAUDE_AGENTS_DIR=$REPO_ROOT/.claude/agents, AUGMENT_AGENTS_DIR=$REPO_ROOT/agent_providers/augment | REPO_ROOT derived from BASH_SOURCE so it is safe to call from any cwd | uses `cp -v` so the transcript is the evidence of what was installed | header and help text still contain {{PROJECT_SHORT}} - this file is itself template-substituted by setup-template.sh (.sh is in its find pattern list) | no dry-run, no uninstall, no idempotency check beyond cp overwrite | the header comment claims '11 agent prompts' but the copy is a wildcard glob with no count check, so the number is a comment not an assertion

concepts.title: pre-release-check.sh - Release Gate
concepts.description: Automates the verifiable items of the pre-release checklist across five gate categories before a release tag is cut.
concepts.notes: scripts/pre-release-check.sh, 209 lines, bash, set -euo pipefail, executable | usage: ./scripts/pre-release-check.sh [version]; VERSION defaults to the literal string UNSET, so forgetting the argument does not abort | cd's to PROJECT_ROOT first, so it always evaluates the repo not the cwd | 5 gate sections: 1 Code Quality Gates (line 44), 2 Documentation Completeness (85), 3 Template Compatibility (124), 4 Backward Compatibility (145), 5 Git State (167) | three-way tally check_pass / check_fail / check_warn incrementing PASS/FAIL/WARN counters | section 1 runs `bash -n scripts/sync-claude-harness.sh` (syntax only, NOT the tests/ suites) and greps for '<<<<<<' merge markers across *.sh *.md *.json *.toml *.yml *.mdc excluding node_modules, .git and the checklist docs themselves | automates docs/release/PRE-RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md | section 2 DOES execute every tests/test-*.sh suite via `timeout 120 bash "$test_file"` (line 66) and calls check_fail for any suite whose output lacks an ALL...PASS marker, so failing suites do block the gate | verified exit logic: FAIL>0 prints RELEASE BLOCKED and exits 1; WARN>0 exits 0 with warnings; otherwise exits 0

concepts.title: generate-changelog.sh - Structured Changelog Generator
concepts.description: Diffs two git refs and emits a schema-v1.0.0 changelog in YAML or Markdown, classifying .claude/ changes into five categories.
concepts.notes: scripts/generate-changelog.sh, 601 lines, bash, set -euo pipefail, executable, 15 functions | usage: --from <ref> --to <ref> [--format yaml|markdown] [--version X.Y.Z] [--help]; OUTPUT_FORMAT defaults to yaml, FROM_REF/TO_REF default empty | emits SCHEMA_VERSION 1.0.0 matching the HARNESS_CHANGELOG.yml schema | pipeline: parse_args -> validate_ref (both refs) -> collect_changes (git diff --name-status) -> classify_file per path -> emit_yaml or emit_markdown, driven by main | classify_file returns one of 5 categories, first match wins: renames (R*) and deletions (D) are ALWAYS BREAKING and override every path rule; .claude/agents/*.md and .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md to METHODOLOGY; .claude/commands/*.md to NEW_FILE if added else UPDATED_FILE; .claude/<top-level>.json and .claude/hooks/* to CONFIG; .claude/<top-level>.md to UPDATED_FILE; any other added file to NEW_FILE; default UPDATED_FILE | classification is .claude/-ONLY: files under .gemini/, .codex/, .cursor/, .agents/ and dark-factory/ - all legal sync domains - fall through to the generic NEW_FILE/UPDATED_FILE default and can never be tagged METHODOLOGY or CONFIG | status_to_change_type maps A/M/D/R* to added/modified/deleted/renamed; is_breaking duplicates the D/R* rule | disables ANSI colours when stdout is not a tty | no test suite covers this script - there is no tests/test-changelog*.sh

concepts.title: reorganize-docs.sh - One-Shot Docs Reorganization
concepts.description: Historical migration that git-mv'd eight root docs into docs/ subdirectories and rewrote every reference to them.
concepts.notes: scripts/reorganize-docs.sh, 344 lines, bash, set -e, executable, no functions - straight-line procedure | ONE-SHOT MIGRATION, already applied: implements docs/REPOSITORY-REORGANIZATION-PLAN.md | preflight refuses to run unless README.md and .git/ are both present in the cwd (must be repo root); warns and prompts on uncommitted changes via git diff-index; a second explicit y/N confirmation is required before proceeding | creates docs/database, docs/security, docs/ci-cd, docs/archive | 8 git mv operations: DATA_DICTIONARY.md, RLS_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md, RLS_POLICY_CATALOG.md, RLS_DATABASE_MIGRATION_SOP.md to docs/database/; SECURITY_FIRST_ARCHITECTURE.md to docs/security/; CI-CD-Pipeline-Guide.md to docs/ci-cd/; README-TEMPLATE.md to docs/archive/; apply-workflow.sh to scripts/ | each move is guarded by an existence test so a re-run is a no-op | deliberately leaves AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in the root per AI-assistant convention | then writes README.md index files for the new directories and rewrites references, overlapping heavily with scripts/update-doc-references.sh and scripts/fix-remaining-doc-references.sh - three scripts editing the same link set | uses git mv, so the moves are staged but not committed; the operator must commit | no dry-run flag

concepts.title: update-doc-references.sh - Doc Link Rewriter
concepts.description: Rewrites markdown links to the six docs moved by the reorganization, taking a .bak backup of every file it edits.
concepts.notes: scripts/update-doc-references.sh, 177 lines, bash, set -e, executable | companion to scripts/reorganize-docs.sh, cited as part of docs/REPOSITORY-REORGANIZATION-PLAN.md | update_file_references() copies each target to <file>.bak, runs one `sed -i.tmp` with 6 -e expressions, removes the .tmp, then diffs against the .bak to report whether anything actually changed | rewrites exactly 6 markdown-link forms: ](DATA_DICTIONARY.md), ](RLS_IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md), ](RLS_POLICY_CATALOG.md), ](RLS_DATABASE_MIGRATION_SOP.md), ](SECURITY_FIRST_ARCHITECTURE.md), ](CI-CD-Pipeline-Guide.md) to their docs/database, docs/security and docs/ci-cd targets | uses `sed -i.tmp` (a suffix is supplied) so it is portable across GNU and BSD sed, unlike apply-workflow.sh and generalize-onboarding-docs.sh | an inline comment notes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md stay in the root | leaves .bak files behind for the operator to clean up | handles ONLY the ](...) markdown-link form - the backtick-quoted `FILE.md` and bare '- FILE.md' list forms are the job of scripts/fix-remaining-doc-references.sh, which is why two scripts exist for one migration

concepts.title: fix-remaining-doc-references.sh - Residual Link Fixer
concepts.description: Second-pass cleanup that rewrites backtick and bare-list doc references missed by the main reference updater.
concepts.notes: scripts/fix-remaining-doc-references.sh, 84 lines, bash, set -e, executable - the smallest script in scripts/ | operates on a hardcoded FILES array of 8 paths: AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/onboarding/DAY-1-CHECKLIST.md, docs/onboarding/META-PROMPTS-FOR-USERS.md, docs/onboarding/USER-JOURNEY-VALIDATION-REPORT.md, docs/onboarding/{{TICKET_PREFIX}}-326-COMPLETION-SUMMARY.md, docs/team/PLANNING-AGENT-META-PROMPT.md, patterns_library/database/rls-migration.md | one entry contains an unsubstituted {{TICKET_PREFIX}} inside a FILENAME - setup-template.sh substitutes file CONTENTS via sed but never renames files, so this path only resolves in a fork whose docs were renamed by hand; guarded by `if [ -f "$file" ]` so it silently skips otherwise | rewrites the same 6 documents as scripts/update-doc-references.sh but in three additional syntactic forms: ](FILE.md), backtick-quoted `FILE.md`, and '- FILE.md' list items | takes a .bak copy per file, uses portable `sed -i.tmp`, cleans up the .tmp | third of three overlapping link-rewriting scripts (with reorganize-docs.sh and update-doc-references.sh) | one-shot historical cleanup, already applied

concepts.title: generalize-onboarding-docs.sh - Onboarding Doc Generalizer
concepts.description: Replaces hardcoded project references in five onboarding docs with template placeholders; uses GNU-only sed.
concepts.notes: scripts/generalize-onboarding-docs.sh, 85 lines, bash, set -euo pipefail, executable | targets 5 files via brace expansion under docs/onboarding/: DAY-1-CHECKLIST.md, SOCIAL-MEDIA-SETUP.md, AGENT-SETUP-GUIDE.md, META-PROMPTS-FOR-USERS.md, USER-JOURNEY-VALIDATION-REPORT.md | backs each up to <file>.bak before editing; update_file() returns 1 with a red 'File not found' message for missing targets | direction is the INVERSE of setup-template.sh: it turns concrete values back INTO {{...}} placeholders, e.g. github.com/{{GITHUB_ORG}}/{{PROJECT_REPO}} becomes {{GITHUB_REPO_URL}}, and '{{PROJECT_SHORT}} SAFe' becomes 'SAFe multi-agent' | ordering matters and is hand-tuned: the longer '{{PROJECT_SHORT}} SAFe Multi-Agent Development' rule runs before the shorter '{{PROJECT_SHORT}} SAFe' rule to avoid a partial rewrite | PORTABILITY DEFECT: uses bare `sed -i 's/.../.../g'` with no backup suffix - GNU-only; on BSD/macOS sed this consumes the next argument as the suffix and errors, and set -euo pipefail then aborts the run mid-file | contrast: scripts/setup-template.sh has a _sed_inplace GNU/BSD shim and update-doc-references.sh uses sed -i.tmp; this script has neither | one-shot maintenance script, not part of any workflow or CI path

concepts.title: generalize_commands.py - Command Template Generalizer
concepts.description: Python utility that injects a template notice, placeholder substitutions, and a customization guide into slash-command markdown.
concepts.notes: scripts/generalize_commands.py, 175 lines, python3, mode 0644 (NOT executable despite the #!/usr/bin/env python3 shebang - must be run as `python3 scripts/generalize_commands.py`) | the ONLY non-bash file in scripts/ | 3 helper functions plus a driver: add_template_notice, replace_patterns, add_customization_guide | BROKEN AS SHIPPED: COMMANDS_DIR is the absolute literal Path('/home/{{AUTHOR_HANDLE}}/Projects/{{PROJECT_REPO}}/.claude/commands') - an author-machine path that setup-template.sh will substitute (.py is in its find pattern list) into a still-absolute /home/<handle>/Projects/<repo> path, which only resolves on a Linux box with that exact layout; there is no repo-root derivation and no CLI argument | add_template_notice splits content on '---' with maxsplit 2 to insert a '> TEMPLATE' banner after the YAML frontmatter, and is idempotent (returns unchanged when the banner marker is already present) | add_customization_guide appends a '## Customization Guide' markdown table of placeholder/description/example rows, also idempotent via a heading check | column padding uses fixed widths (17, 30, 32) with naive `' ' * (N - len(x))`, so any placeholder or description longer than its budget yields a negative repeat count and an unaligned row | operates on .claude/commands/*.md only - no other provider's command directory | one-shot authoring tool, not referenced by any test or workflow
